correctness.rationale: For every h>0 (q in (0,1)), six explicit column-stochastic matrices contract zero-sum vectors uniformly. Cyclic symmetry forces the random-order stationary mean u and covariance VΠ/2. Direct expansion yields a(q), b(q), and V=b/(1-a), with D(q)>0. The two cyclic fixed-order classes have exactly the stated fixed points and biases. Exact factorizations of V-B_min and V-B_max, positivity of D and T, and strict monotonicity F′>0 prove a unique crossover and the complete all-h ordering. A packaged SymPy verifier reconstructs the operators and identities; finite rational tests are supplementary, not universal proof.

originality.rationale: The new object is a stationary distribution over three-component probability vectors generated by independently reordered exact Markov edge subflows. The inspected graph-Laplacian integrator paper supplies the method, long-time Markov-splitting literature provides different relative-entropy diagnostics, and quantum randomized product formulas concern unitary finite-time approximation. Targeted indexed-literature and claim-level searches found no statement implying this exact six-order stationary covariance and sharp sign reversal. Literature incompleteness and alternative generic random affine recursions remain genuine risks, not proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: At fixed cost of three positive stochastic edge exponentials per step, randomization improves stationary Euclidean squared error from the optimal fixed-order order h² to order h³ for small h, but loses to the best fixed order after an exact nontrivial threshold. It gives an exact minimal noncommutative graph-Laplacian counterexample to global dominance of randomized versus fixed ordering, and a practical step-size decision boundary. The natural comparison is a stationary solver of an invariant Markov distribution, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
